name: @dpesch/mantisbt-mcp-server

tools.name: get_issue
tools.description:
Retrieve one MantisBT issue by "id", or several by "ids" (1–50). Pass exactly one of the two.

With "id": returns the issue with all fields including notes (each with view_url), attachments and relationships, unless "select" is given.
With "ids": returns { issues, requested, found, failed } — requests run in parallel (max 5 concurrent); missing or inaccessible IDs give null at their position instead of failing the call.

Use "select" to fetch only some fields, e.g. select: "notes" for just the notes or select: "attachments" for just the file attachments of an issue.

id.description: Numeric issue ID (use either id or ids)

ids.description: Several issue IDs (1–50) to fetch in one call (use either id or ids)

select.description: Comma-separated list of fields to include in the response (server-side projection, same as list_issues). Significantly reduces response size. Example: "id,summary,status,notes"

tools.name: get_issues
tools.description:
Deprecated: use get_issue with ids instead — get_issues will be removed in 2.0.0.

Retrieve multiple MantisBT issues by their numeric IDs in a single MCP call. Requests run in parallel (max 5 concurrent). Missing or inaccessible IDs return null at their array position — the call never fails due to individual missing IDs. Response includes "requested", "found", and "failed" counters for quick validation.

ids.description: Array of numeric issue IDs to fetch (1–50). null is returned per ID on 404/403/error instead of failing the whole call.

tools.name: list_issues
tools.description:
List MantisBT issues with optional filtering. Returns a paginated list of issues. Use the "select" parameter to limit returned fields and reduce response size significantly.

Note: "assigned_to", "reporter_id", "status", and date filters are applied client-side (the MantisBT REST API does not support these as server-side filters). When any of these filters are active the tool automatically fetches multiple pages internally until enough matching results are found (up to 500 issues scanned); if that limit ends the search before the page is full, the response contains "truncated": true. The "page" and "page_size" parameters refer to the resulting filtered list.

Tip for date queries: fetching with select="id,updated_at,created_at" plus a date filter is very compact and efficient.

For overviews use "group_by" ("status", "handler", "priority" or "category"): the server counts all matching issues itself and returns { group_by, total, groups: [{ id, name, label?, count }] } instead of an issue list — far fewer tokens than listing issues and counting them. All filters still apply. If the scan stops at its limit (50,000 issues), the response contains "truncated": true.

filter_id.description: Use a saved MantisBT filter ID

select.description: Comma-separated list of fields to include in the response (server-side projection). Significantly reduces response size. Example: "id,summary,status,priority,handler,updated_at"

status.description: Filter issues by status name (e.g. "new", "feedback", "acknowledged", "confirmed", "assigned", "resolved", "closed") or use "open" as shorthand for all statuses with id < 80 (i.e. not yet resolved or closed). Applied client-side after fetching — when combined with pagination, a page may contain fewer results than page_size.

group_by.description: Return counts per group instead of issues: "status", "handler", "priority" or "category". All matching issues are counted (page, page_size and select are ignored).

updated_after.description: ISO-8601 timestamp — only return issues updated after this date (exclusive). Example: "2026-03-25T00:00:00Z"

updated_before.description: ISO-8601 timestamp — only return issues updated before this date (exclusive). Example: "2026-03-28T00:00:00Z"

created_after.description: ISO-8601 timestamp — only return issues created after this date (exclusive). Example: "2026-03-01T00:00:00Z"

created_before.description: ISO-8601 timestamp — only return issues created before this date (exclusive). Example: "2026-03-15T00:00:00Z"

tools.name: create_issue
tools.description:
Create a new MantisBT issue. Returns the full created issue object including the assigned id, summary, status, priority, severity, category, reporter, created_at, and view_url.

Required fields: summary, description, project_id, category. All other fields are optional with sensible defaults (priority: "normal", severity: "minor").

Recommended workflow:
1. Call get_project with include: ["categories"] to obtain a valid category name
2. Optionally add "versions" to include to obtain version names
3. Optionally call get_project with member_query to resolve the assignee's username

Both priority and severity accept canonical English names or localized labels from the connected MantisBT instance — call get_issue_schema to see all available values.

For the handler, prefer the username field (resolved server-side) over handler_id when working interactively.

description.description: Detailed issue description (required). Do not create issues without a description. Plain text or Markdown.

project_id.description: Project ID the issue belongs to — use list_projects to discover project IDs

category.description: Category name (required). Use get_project with include: ["categories"] to list available categories for the project.

priority.description: Priority level. Canonical English names: none, low, normal, high, urgent, immediate. Default: "normal". Use get_issue_schema to see localized labels.

severity.description: Severity level. Canonical English names: feature, trivial, text, tweak, minor, major, crash, block. Default: "minor". Use get_issue_schema to see localized labels.

handler_id.description: Numeric user ID of the assignee. Alternative to the handler field — use one or the other, not both.

handler.description: MantisBT login name of the assignee. The server resolves the name to a user ID from the project member list. Use get_project with member_query or include: ["users"] to look up valid login names.

version.description: Affected product version name. Use get_project with include: ["versions"] to list available version names for the project.

target_version.description: Target fix version — version in which the issue is planned to be resolved. Use get_project with include: ["versions"] to list available version names.

fixed_in_version.description: Version in which the issue was fixed. Use get_project with include: ["versions"] to list available version names.

steps_to_reproduce.description: Step-by-step instructions to reproduce the issue. Plain text or Markdown.

additional_information.description: Additional context or notes about the issue. Plain text or Markdown.

reproducibility.description: How reliably the issue reproduces. Canonical English names: always, sometimes, random, have not tried, unable to reproduce, N/A. Use get_issue_schema to see localized labels.

view_state.description: Visibility of the issue: "public" (visible to all, default) or "private" (restricted to higher-access users).

custom_fields.description: Custom field values: [{field: {id|name}, value: "<string>"}]. Use get_issue_schema or get_metadata to discover available custom fields per project.

field.description: Custom field reference: { id } or { name }

tools.name: update_issue

add_monitors.description: MantisBT login names to add as monitors (watchers) of the issue

remove_monitors.description: MantisBT login names to remove from the monitors of the issue; names that are not monitoring are ignored

dry_run.description: If true, return the patch payload that would be sent without actually updating the issue. Useful for previewing changes before committing them.

note.description: Optional note text appended after a successful update (e.g. reason for a status change). Replaces a separate add_note call.

note_view_state.description: Visibility of the appended note: "public" (default) or "private". Only used when "note" is set.

fields.description: Fields to update (partial update — only provided fields are changed; unknown keys are rejected). May be omitted when only add_monitors, remove_monitors or note are given.

field.description: Custom field reference: { id } or { name }

id.description: ID of the note to edit (from get_issue)

view_state.description: New visibility; omitted = keep the current one

tools.name: delete_issue
tools.description: Permanently delete a MantisBT issue. This action is irreversible.

tools.name: list_notes
tools.description:
Deprecated: use get_issue with select: "notes" instead — list_notes will be removed in 2.0.0.

List all notes (comments) attached to a MantisBT issue.

tools.name: add_note
tools.description:
Add a note (comment) to an existing MantisBT issue. Returns the created note object including id, created_at, reporter, text, view_state, and a view_url linking directly to the note in the MantisBT web UI.

Full UTF-8 text is supported. Markdown syntax is stored as-is — rendering depends on the MantisBT instance's configured text renderer.

Use view_state="private" to restrict the note to users with reporter-level access or higher; public notes are visible to all users who can view the issue.

Prerequisites: obtain issue_id from list_issues, get_issue, or search_issues.

issue_id.description: Numeric issue ID — use list_issues or get_issue to obtain issue IDs

text.description: Note text (minimum 1 character). Full UTF-8 including emoji is supported. Markdown is stored as-is.

view_state.description: Visibility of the note: "public" (visible to all, default) or "private" (visible only to users with sufficient access level).

tools.name: delete_note
tools.description:
Permanently delete a note from a MantisBT issue. This action is irreversible — deleted notes cannot be recovered.

Returns a plain-text confirmation message on success. Returns an error if the note does not exist or the current user lacks permission to delete it (MantisBT enforces access control: users can typically only delete their own notes unless they have manager-level access or higher).

Prerequisites: obtain note_id from get_issue (notes[].id).

issue_id.description: Numeric issue ID that owns the note

note_id.description: Numeric note ID to delete — obtain from get_issue (notes[].id)

tools.name: list_issue_files
tools.description:
Deprecated: use get_issue with select: "attachments" instead — list_issue_files will be removed in 2.0.0.

List all file attachments of a MantisBT issue. Returns an array of attachment objects, each containing id, filename, size in bytes, content_type, and download_url. Returns an empty array if the issue has no attachments.

tools.name: upload_file
tools.description:
Upload a file as an attachment to a MantisBT issue. Adds the file to the issue without modifying any issue fields or status. Returns the created attachment metadata on success.

Provide exactly one of the two input modes:
- file_path (preferred): absolute path to a local file — use this whenever the file exists on disk; the server reads and encodes it automatically; filename is derived from the path. Note: file_path reads from the server's filesystem and is disabled over the HTTP transport unless MANTIS_UPLOAD_DIR is configured — HTTP clients should use content instead.
- content: Base64-encoded file content — only use this when the file is not accessible via a path (e.g. in-memory data); filename must be supplied explicitly via the filename parameter

The optional content_type sets the MIME type (e.g. "image/png"); defaults to "application/octet-stream". Use the optional description to annotate the attachment.

Use this tool to attach files such as logs, screenshots, or patches to an existing issue. To list existing attachments, use get_issue with select: "attachments".

file_path.description: Preferred: absolute path to the local file to upload — use this whenever the file exists on disk (mutually exclusive with content)

content.description: Fallback: Base64-encoded file content — only use when file_path is not available (mutually exclusive with file_path)

filename.description: File name for the attachment (required when using content; overrides the derived name when using file_path)

content_type.description: MIME type of the file, e.g. "image/png" (default: "application/octet-stream")

tools.name: add_relationship
tools.description:
Add a relationship between two MantisBT issues.

Relationship types — use either type_id (numeric) or type_name (string):
- 0 / "duplicate_of"  — this issue is a duplicate of target
- 1   / "related_to"    — this issue is related to target
- 2    / "parent_of"     — this issue depends on target (target must be done first); alias: "depends_on"
- 3     / "child_of"      — this issue blocks target (target can't proceed until this is done); alias: "blocks"
- 4 / "has_duplicate" — this issue has target as a duplicate

Directionality note: "A child_of B" means A blocks B. "A parent_of B" means A depends on B.

Dash variants (e.g. "related-to") are also accepted for type_name.

issue_id.description: The source issue ID (the one the relationship is added to)

type_id.description: Relationship type ID: 0=duplicate_of, 1=related_to, 2=parent_of (depends on), 3=child_of (blocks), 4=has_duplicate. Use either type_id or type_name.

type_name.description: Relationship type name as alternative to type_id. Accepted: "duplicate_of", "related_to", "parent_of" (or "depends_on"), "child_of" (or "blocks"), "has_duplicate". Dash variants (e.g. "related-to") also work.

tools.name: remove_relationship
tools.description:
Remove a relationship from a MantisBT issue.

Use get_issue first to retrieve the relationship IDs. The relationship_id is the numeric id field of a relationship object in the issue's relationships array (not the type ID).

issue_id.description: The issue ID the relationship belongs to

relationship_id.description: The numeric ID of the relationship to remove (from the relationships array in get_issue)

tools.name: add_monitor
tools.description:
Deprecated: use update_issue with add_monitors instead — add_monitor will be removed in 2.0.0.

Add a user as a monitor (watcher) of a MantisBT issue. Monitors receive email notifications whenever the issue is updated. Returns { success, monitors } — "monitors" lists the login names now monitoring the issue.

Use it to subscribe team members to issue updates without assigning them as the handler.

Adding a user who is already a monitor is a no-op — the operation succeeds without creating duplicates.

Prerequisites: obtain issue_id from list_issues or get_issue; use get_project with member_query to look up valid MantisBT login names.

issue_id.description: Numeric issue ID — use list_issues or get_issue to obtain issue IDs

username.description: MantisBT login name (not the display name) of the user to add as monitor. Use get_project with member_query to discover valid login names for a project.

tools.name: remove_monitor
tools.description:
Deprecated: use update_issue with remove_monitors instead — remove_monitor will be removed in 2.0.0.

Remove a user from the monitor list of a MantisBT issue. The user will no longer receive email notifications for updates to this issue.

Returns { success, removed, monitors } — "monitors" lists the login names still monitoring the issue. If the user was not a monitor, the call succeeds with removed=false and nothing is changed.

Removing another user requires the monitor_delete_others_bug_threshold access level; without it the call returns an error.

username.description: MantisBT login name (not the display name) of the monitor to remove

tools.name: get_project
tools.description:
Get one MantisBT project: its master data (id, name, description, status, enabled, view_state, access_level, subprojects) and, on request, its categories, users and versions in the same call.

- include: any of "categories", "users", "versions" (default: none — master data only).
- categories: names come without the "[All Projects] " prefix, ready for create_issue / update_issue.
- users: id, name (login name), real_name, email, access_level. access_level returns only users at or above that level (10=viewer, 25=reporter, 40=updater, 55=developer, 70=manager, 90=administrator) and implies include "users".
- member_query: case-insensitive substring search in login name, real name and email; returns all matching users. Implies include "users".
- versions: id, name, released, obsolete, timestamp. obsolete=true adds obsolete versions, inherit=true adds versions of parent projects; either implies include "versions".

Users come from the local metadata cache when it is fresh and no access_level is given. Prerequisites: obtain project_id from list_projects.

project_id.description: Numeric project ID — use list_projects to discover project IDs

access_level.description: Only users at or above this access level; implies include "users"

member_query.description: Case-insensitive substring to find users by login name, real name or email; implies include "users"

obsolete.description: Also return obsolete versions; implies include "versions"

inherit.description: Also return versions inherited from parent projects; implies include "versions"

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List all MantisBT projects accessible to the current API user.

tools.name: get_project_users
tools.description:
Deprecated: use get_project with include: ["users"] instead — get_project_users will be removed in 2.0.0.

List all users with access to a specific MantisBT project. Returns an array of user objects, each containing id, name (login name), real_name, email, and access_level fields.

Access level IDs: 10=viewer, 25=reporter, 40=updater, 55=developer, 70=manager, 90=administrator.

Prerequisites: obtain project_id from list_projects.

project_id.description: Numeric project ID — use list_projects to discover project IDs

access_level.description: Return only users at or above this access level. Common values: 10=viewer, 25=reporter, 40=updater, 55=developer, 70=manager, 90=administrator. Omit to return all users.

tools.name: get_project_versions
tools.description:
Deprecated: use get_project with include: ["versions"] instead — get_project_versions will be removed in 2.0.0.

List all versions defined for a MantisBT project. Returns an array of version objects, each containing id, name, released (boolean), obsolete (boolean), and timestamp (version date). To create, change, release or delete versions use create_version, update_version, release_version and delete_version.

Use the returned version names directly when creating or updating issues via create_issue and update_issue (version, target_version, fixed_in_version fields).

By default, obsolete and inherited parent-project versions are excluded. Set obsolete=true to include deprecated versions; set inherit=true to also return versions from parent projects.

Prerequisites: obtain project_id from list_projects.

project_id.description: Numeric project ID — use list_projects to discover project IDs

obsolete.description: Include obsolete (deprecated) versions in the response. Default: false. Set to true to see all versions including those no longer actively used.

inherit.description: Include versions inherited from parent projects. Default: false. Set to true for sub-projects that share versions with a parent project.

tools.name: get_project_categories
tools.description:
Deprecated: use get_project with include: ["categories"] instead — get_project_categories will be removed in 2.0.0.

List all categories available for a MantisBT project.

Note: The MantisBT API returns global (cross-project) categories with a "[All Projects] " prefix.
This tool strips that prefix so the returned names can be used directly when creating issues.

tools.name: find_project_member
tools.description:
Deprecated: use get_project with member_query instead — find_project_member will be removed in 2.0.0.

Search for users with access to a MantisBT project by name, display name, or email.

Returns up to `limit` matching users (default: 10, max: 100). Matching is case-insensitive substring search across `name`, `real_name`, and `email` fields. Omit `query` to list the first `limit` users.

Data is served from the local metadata cache when fresh; falls back to a live API call otherwise.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring to match against name, real_name, or email

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 10, max: 100)

tools.name: create_version
tools.description:
Create a new version in a MantisBT project. Returns the created version object (id, name, description, released, obsolete, timestamp).

Version names must be unique within the project. Without timestamp, MantisBT uses the current date.

Requires the manage_project_threshold access level in the project (MantisBT default: manager).

project_id.description: Numeric ID of the project the version belongs to — use list_projects to discover project IDs

released.description: Mark the version as released. MantisBT default: false

obsolete.description: Mark the version as obsolete. MantisBT default: false

timestamp.description: Version date as ISO 8601 string, e.g. "2026-09-27" or "2026-09-27T10:00:00+02:00". Determines the order in roadmap and changelog.

tools.name: update_version
tools.description:
Update an existing version of a MantisBT project. Only the fields you pass are changed. Returns the updated version object.

Renaming a version also rewrites the version, target_version and fixed_in_version fields of all issues that reference it (including subprojects if versions are inherited).

Setting released=true does not change the version date — pass timestamp as well (e.g. the release date).

To release a version: released=true, timestamp=<release date>, and optionally next_version=<name> to create the follow-up version in the same call. With next_version the response is { version: <updated>, next_version: <created> } — or next_version_error: <message> if creating the follow-up failed (the update itself stays in effect). Without next_version the response is the updated version object.

The version must belong to project_id itself: versions inherited from a parent project can only be changed via the parent's project_id (otherwise MantisBT answers "Version not found"). get_project with include: ["versions"] and without inherit lists the project's own versions.

Requires the manage_project_threshold access level in the project (MantisBT default: manager).

project_id.description: Numeric ID of the project the version belongs to — use list_projects to discover project IDs

version_id.description: Numeric version ID — use get_project with include: ["versions"] to discover version IDs

name.description: New version name (must be unique within the project)

timestamp.description: Version date as ISO 8601 string, e.g. "2026-09-27" or "2026-09-27T10:00:00+02:00". Determines the order in roadmap and changelog.

next_version.description: Only with released=true: name of a follow-up version to create as unreleased placeholder, e.g. "1.2.1". Used as-is — no automatic numbering.

tools.name: release_version
tools.description:
Deprecated: use update_version with released=true, timestamp and (optionally) next_version instead — release_version will be removed in 2.0.0.

Mark a version as released and set its date (default: now). Optionally create a follow-up version in the same step.

The follow-up version is only created when next_version is given; its name is used as-is — no automatic numbering.

Returns { released: <version> } plus either next_version: <version> or next_version_error: <message>. The two steps are separate API calls: if creating the follow-up version fails, the release itself stays in effect and the error is reported in next_version_error.

The version must belong to project_id itself: versions inherited from a parent project can only be changed via the parent's project_id (otherwise MantisBT answers "Version not found"). get_project with include: ["versions"] and without inherit lists the project's own versions.

Requires the manage_project_threshold access level in the project (MantisBT default: manager).

project_id.description: Numeric ID of the project the version belongs to — use list_projects to discover project IDs

version_id.description: Numeric version ID — use get_project with include: ["versions"] to discover version IDs

timestamp.description: Release date as ISO 8601 string. Default: now.

next_version.description: Name of a follow-up version to create as unreleased placeholder, e.g. "1.2.1". Omit to only release.

tools.name: delete_version
tools.description:
Permanently delete a version of a MantisBT project. This action is irreversible.

MantisBT clears the version, target_version and fixed_in_version fields of all issues that reference the deleted version (including subprojects if versions are inherited). To retire a version without touching issues, set obsolete=true via update_version instead.

The version must belong to project_id itself: versions inherited from a parent project can only be changed via the parent's project_id (otherwise MantisBT answers "Version not found"). get_project with include: ["versions"] and without inherit lists the project's own versions.

Requires the manage_project_threshold access level in the project (MantisBT default: manager).

project_id.description: Numeric ID of the project the version belongs to — use list_projects to discover project IDs

version_id.description: Numeric version ID — use get_project with include: ["versions"] to discover version IDs

tools.name: get_current_user
tools.description:
Retrieve the profile of the user associated with the current API key: id, name (login name), real_name, email, language, timezone, access_level, created_at and the accessible projects.

"language" is the MantisBT language of this user (e.g. "german", "english") — use it as the hint for which language to write issue texts and notes in, and expect localized enum labels in that language.

tools.name: list_filters
tools.description: List all saved MantisBT issue filters accessible to the current user. Filter IDs can be used with list_issues.

tools.name: get_config
tools.description:
Retrieve one or more MantisBT configuration options.

Common option names:
- "status_enum_string" — issue status values and their IDs
- "priority_enum_string" — priority values
- "severity_enum_string" — severity values
- "resolution_enum_string" — resolution values
- "reproducibility_enum_string" — reproducibility values
- "view_state_enum_string" — view state values
- "access_levels_enum_string" — access level values

options.description: Array of configuration option names to retrieve

tools.name: get_issue_enums
tools.description:
Deprecated: use get_issue_schema instead — get_issue_enums will be removed in 2.0.0.

Return valid ID, name, and (if available) localized label for all issue enum fields.

Use this tool before creating or updating issues to look up the correct value
for severity, status, priority, resolution, or reproducibility.

Example response (English installation):
{
  "severity":         [{"id": 10, "name": "feature"}, {"id": 50, "name": "minor"}, ...],
  "status":           [{"id": 10, "name": "new"}, {"id": 20, "name": "feedback"}, ...],
  "priority":         [{"id": 10, "name": "none"}, {"id": 30, "name": "normal"}, ...],
  "resolution":       [{"id": 10, "name": "open"}, {"id": 20, "name": "fixed"}, ...],
  "reproducibility":  [{"id": 10, "name": "always"}, {"id": 70, "name": "have not tried"}, ...]
}

Example response (localized installation, e.g. German):
{
  "status": [
    {"id": 10, "name": "new",      "label": "Neu"},
    {"id": 20, "name": "feedback", "label": "Feedback"},
    {"id": 30, "name": "acknowledged", "label": "Bestätigt"},
    ...
  ],
  ...
}

Fields:
- "id"             — numeric ID accepted by the API
- "name"           — localized or canonical name from the MantisBT database
- "label"          — UI display label (only present when it differs from "name")
- "canonical_name" — English canonical name (only present on localized installs)

For create_issue (severity, priority, reproducibility): pass the canonical English name, the
localized "name", or the "label" — all are accepted. The server resolves them to the correct ID.

For update_issue: pass either "id" or "name" in the field reference object.

Note: on some installations enum values are customized at the database level. In that case "name"
itself may be localized (e.g. "kleinerer Fehler" instead of "minor") and no "label" will be present
because there is no separate English original.

tools.name: list_languages
tools.description:
Deprecated: use get_current_user (field "language") instead — list_languages will be removed in 2.0.0.

Despite its name, MantisBT's GET /lang returns only the language of the current user ({ strings, language }), not a list of all languages.

tools.name: list_tags
tools.description:
List all tags defined in the MantisBT installation.

The MantisBT REST API exposes a GET /tags endpoint on some installations.
If that endpoint is not available, this tool falls back to the local metadata
cache populated by get_metadata.

tools.name: sync_metadata
tools.description:
Deprecated: use get_metadata with refresh: true instead — sync_metadata will be removed in 2.0.0.

Fetch all projects and their associated users, versions, categories, and tags from MantisBT and store them in the local metadata cache.

Tags are fetched via the dedicated GET /tags endpoint when available. On installations where that endpoint is missing (MantisBT < 2.26), tags are collected by scanning all issues across all projects.

This is useful for getting a complete overview of your MantisBT installation.
The cache is valid for 24 hours by default (configurable via MANTIS_CACHE_TTL env var).
Use this tool to refresh stale data.

tools.name: get_metadata
tools.description:
Return the cached MantisBT metadata (projects with their users, versions and categories, plus all tags).

- detail: "summary" (default) — compact counts: project count, tag count, per-project counts of users, versions and categories, cached_at, ttl_seconds.
- detail: "full" — the complete raw cache with all lists (large; minified JSON).
- refresh: true — re-fetch everything from MantisBT before answering (otherwise the cache is used and only synced when missing or expired; default TTL 24 hours).

When semantic search is enabled, the response also contains "search_index": how many issues are indexed vs. the total, and the time of the last sync.

For lists of a single project use get_project with include; for tags use list_tags.

detail.description: "summary" (default): counts only; "full": the complete raw cache

refresh.description: Re-fetch all metadata from MantisBT first (default: false)

tools.name: get_metadata_full
tools.description:
Deprecated: use get_metadata with detail: "full" instead — get_metadata_full will be removed in 2.0.0.

Return the complete raw MantisBT metadata cache: all projects with full fields, and per-project lists of users, versions, categories, plus all tags.

If the cache does not exist or has expired (default TTL: 24 hours), it will automatically sync first.
Use get_metadata with refresh: true to force a refresh.

tools.name: get_issue_fields
tools.description:
Deprecated: use get_issue_schema instead — get_issue_fields will be removed in 2.0.0.

Return all field names that are valid for the "select" parameter of list_issues and get_issue.

Fields are discovered by fetching a sample issue from MantisBT (which reflects the server's active configuration — e.g. whether eta, projection, or profile fields are enabled) and merging the result with fields that MantisBT omits when empty (notes, attachments, relationships, etc.). The result is cached with the same TTL as the metadata cache.

Use this tool before constructing a "select" string to ensure you only request fields that exist on this server.

project_id.description: Optional project ID to scope the sample issue fetch

tools.name: get_issue_schema
tools.description:
Return what is valid for issues on this MantisBT server, in one response:

- fields: all field names valid for the "select" parameter of get_issue, list_issues and search_issues. Discovered from a sample issue (reflects the server's active configuration) plus fields MantisBT omits when empty (notes, attachments, relationships, …); cached with the metadata TTL. fields_source tells where they came from: "cache", "live" or "static".
- enums: ID, name and (if available) localized label for severity, status, priority, resolution and reproducibility. "name" or "id" is what create_issue / update_issue accept; "canonical_name" appears on localized installations.

Call it before building a "select" string or before setting enum fields.

project_id.description: Optional project ID to scope the sample issue used for field discovery

tools.name: attach_tags
tools.description:
Attach one or more tags to a MantisBT issue.

Each tag can be specified either by ID or by name. If a tag name is provided
that does not exist yet, MantisBT will create it automatically (requires
tag_create_threshold permission, default: REPORTER).

Requires tag_attach_threshold permission (default: REPORTER).

tags.description: Tags to attach — each entry needs at least id or name

tools.name: detach_tag
tools.description:
Remove a tag from a MantisBT issue.

Requires tag_detach_own_threshold (default: REPORTER) for own tags,
or tag_detach_threshold (default: DEVELOPER) for tags attached by others.
